synopsis: The Amazon six-pager is a six-page narrative memo, described as a sibling of Amazon’s working backwards method and read silently at the start of a meeting instead of slides [f16458]. Chapter 12 identifies it as a documented template suitable for structuring the heavy off-road collision mitigation validation plan [f9980]. The chapter also recommends a shorter, 1–2-page executive decision brief drawing on BLUF, six-pager and Heilmeier templates or sources, distinguishing the brief from the full six-page memo [f10152, f16458]. These are recommendations about presentation structure, not demonstrated effectiveness: the corpus found no evidence that six-pagers, BLUF or the Pyramid Principle improve approval or success and classifies them as popular but unproven [f10141].

relations.note: Defines the narrative format and meeting practice of the recommended template.
Adds a shorter executive brief drawing on the six-pager among other sources.
Qualifies recommended suitability: improved approval or success remains unproven.
Recommended presentation sources include methods whose effectiveness remains unproven.
